statement: The square on a rational straight line, if applied to an apotome, produces as, breadth the binomial straight line the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the apotome and in the same ratio; and further the binomial so arising has the same order as the apotome.
heath_proof: Let A be a rational straight line and BD an apotome, and let the rectangle BD, KH be equal to the square on A, so that the square on the rational straight line A when applied to the apotome BD produces KH as breadth; I say that KH is a binomial straight line the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of BD and in the same ratio; and further KH has the same order as BD. For let DC be the annex to BD; therefore BC, CD are rational straight lines commensurable in square only. [X. 73] Let the rectangle BC, G be also equal to the square on A. But the square on A is rational; therefore the rectangle BC, G is also rational. And it has been applied to the rational straight line BC; therefore G is rational and commensurable in length with BC. [X. 20] Since now the rectangle BC, G is equal to the rectangle BD, KH, therefore, proportionally, as CB is to BD, so is KH to G. [VI. 16] But BC is greater than BD; therefore KH is also greater than G. [V. 16, V. 14] Let KE be made equal to G; therefore KE is commensurable in length with BC. And since, as CB is to BD, so is HK to KE, therefore, convertendo, as BC is to CD, so is KH to HE. [V. 19] Let it be contrived that, as KH is to HE, so is HF to FE; therefore also the remainder KF is to FH as KH is to HE, that is, as BC is to CD. [V. 19] But BC, CD are commensurable in square only; therefore KF, FH are also commensurable in square only. [X. 11] And since, as KH is to HE, so is KF to FH, while, as KH is to HE, so is HF to FE, therefore also, as KF is to FH, so is HF to FE, [V. 11] so that also, as the first is to the third, so is the square on the first to the square on the second; [V. Def. 9] therefore also, as KF is to FE, so is the square on KF to the square on FH. But the square on KF is commensurable with the square on FH, for KF, FH are commensurable in square; therefore KF is also commensurable in length with FE, [X. 11] so that KF is also commensurable in length with KE. [X. 15] But KE is rational and commensurable in length with BC; therefore KF is also rational and commensurable in length with BC. [X. 12] And, since, as BC is to CD, so is KF to FH, alternately, as BC is to KF, so is DC to FH. [V. 16] But BC is commensurable with KF; therefore FH is also commensurable in length with CD. [X. 11] But BC, CD are rational straight lines commensurable in square only; therefore KF, FH are also rational straight lines [X. Def. 3] commensurable in square only; therefore KH is binomial. [X. 36] If now the square on BC is greater than the square on CD by the square on a straight line commensurable with BC, the square on KF will also be greater than the square on FH by the square on a straight line commensurable with KF. [X 14] And, if BC is commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, so also is KF; if CD is commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out, so also is FH, but, if neither of the straight lines BC, CD, then neither of the straight lines KF, FH. But, if the square on BC is greater than the square on CD by the square on a straight line incommensurable with BC, the square on KF is also greater than the square on FH by the square on a straight line incommensurable with KF. [X. 14] And, if BC is commensurable with the rational straight line set out, so also is KF; if CD is so commensurable, in length with the rational straight line set out, so also is FH; but, if neither of the straight lines BC, CD, then neither of the straight lines KF, FH. Therefore KH is a binomial straight line, the terms of which KF, FH are commensurable with the terms BC, CD of the apotome and in the same ratio, and further KH has the same order as BD.
ai_proof_text:
10.113
**Statement:** The square on a rational straight line, if applied to an apotome, produces as, breadth the binomial straight line the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the apotome and in the same ratio; and further the binomial so arising has the same order as the apotome.

**Step 1.** Let A be a rational straight line, and let BD be an apotome, with BG and GD as its terms, so that BD = BG - GD, where BG is the greater term. We must show that when the square on A is applied to BD, the resulting breadth is a binomial straight line whose terms are commensurable with BG and GD respectively, in the same ratio, and of the same order as the apotome BD.

**Step 2.** Apply the square on A to the apotome BD, producing breadth KH, so that the rectangle BD times KH equals the square on A. We seek to determine the nature of KH.

**Step 3.** Since BG and GD are the terms of the apotome BD, BG and GD are rational straight lines commensurable in square only, by the definition of an apotome (D10.3.1 through D10.3.6, and 10.73).

**Step 4.** Apply the square on A to BG, producing as breadth KE, so that the rectangle BG times KE equals the square on A. Since A is rational and BG is rational (being a term of the apotome), and BG is a term of a rational straight line commensurable in square only pair, the square on A applied to BG gives KE, which is rational and commensurable in length with A, by 10.20 (if BG is commensurable in length with A) or rational and commensurable at least in square with A.

**Step 5.** Now consider that BD times KH = the square on A = BG times KE. Since BD = BG - GD, we have (BG - GD) times KH = BG times KE, which gives BG times KH - GD times KH = BG times KE. Therefore BG times (KH - KE) = GD times KH. Let EH = KH - KE, so that KH = KE + EH. Then BG times EH = GD times KH, by CN3 and CN1.

**Step 6.** From BG times EH = GD times KH, we obtain BG : GD = KH : EH, by 6.16. Since BG and GD are commensurable in square only (being terms of the apotome), BG and GD are incommensurable in length. Therefore KH and EH are also incommensurable in length, by 10.11.

**Step 7.** Also from BG : GD = KH : EH, we get by conversion of the ratio (5.19, separando/componendo): BG : BD = KH : KE. That is, since BD = BG - GD and KE = KH - EH, we have BG : (BG - GD) = KH : (KH - EH), giving BG : BD = KH : KE.

**Step 8.** Since BG is commensurable in square with GD (they are rational and commensurable in square only), the square on BG is commensurable with the square on GD. The square on BG has to the square on GD the same ratio as the square on KH has to the square on EH (since BG : GD = KH : EH, by Step 6, the duplicate ratio gives sq(BG) : sq(GD) = sq(KH) : sq(EH), by 6.22). Therefore the square on KH is commensurable with the square on EH, by 10.11. So KH and EH are commensurable in square.

**Step 9.** Since KH and EH are commensurable in square but incommensurable in length (Steps 8 and 6), KH and EH are commensurable in square only.

**Step 10.** We now show that KE and EH are each rational. Since BD times KH = the square on A, and A is rational, the rectangle BD times KH is a rational area. Now BG times KE = the square on A as well (by construction in Step 4). Since A is rational and BG is rational, the rectangle BG times KE is rational. By 10.20, KE is rational and commensurable in length with A (taking the appropriate commensurability conditions from BG's relationship to A).

**Step 11.** From BG : GD = KH : EH (Step 6), we also get the squares: sq(BG) : sq(GD) = sq(KH) : sq(EH), by 6.22. Now KE is rational (Step 10). We show EH is rational. Since GD times KH = BG times EH (Step 5), and GD is rational, and KH has been shown to involve rational relationships, we need to verify EH is rational. From BG : GD = KH : EH and both BG and GD being rational, and KH being expressible in terms of rational quantities, KH and EH are both rational. Specifically, since BG times KE = A^2 is rational, and GD times (KE + EH) = GD times KH, and BG times EH = GD times KH, we can derive: GD times KH = BG times EH, so the rectangle GD times KH is rational (since GD is rational and KH's rectangle with BD gives a rational area). Apply the square on A to GD to get a breadth, say L, so GD times L = A^2 = BG times KE. This gives L rational. Since GD times KH = BG times EH, and BG times KE = GD times L, we can establish that EH is rational by the chain of proportions.

**Step 12.** Since KH and EH are rational and commensurable in square only (Step 9), the straight line KE = KH - EH... but we need KH = KE + EH to form a binomial. We have KH = KE + EH where KE and EH are such that KH and EH are commensurable in square only. Actually, reconsider: we need to show that KH is a binomial with terms KE and EH. Since BG times KE = the square on A and BD times KH = the square on A, we have BD times KH = BG times KE. Since BD < BG (BD is BG minus GD), KH > KE. So KH = KE + EH for some EH > 0.

**Step 13.** Now we show KE and EH are the terms of a binomial. From BD times KH = BG times KE (both equal to A^2), we get BD : BG = KE : KH, by 6.16. Since BG and BD are commensurable in square (sq(BG) is commensurable with sq(BD) through the rational relationships), KE and KH are also commensurable in square by 10.11. From BG times EH = GD times KH (Step 5), we get EH : KH = GD : BG, by 6.16. So GD : BG = EH : KH, and since BG : GD = KH : EH.

**Step 14.** We now verify the terms are commensurable with the terms of the apotome and in the same ratio. From BG : GD = KH : EH (Step 6), the terms KH and EH of the breadth are in the same ratio as BG and GD. Since BG times KE = the square on A = BD times KH, and KE = KH - EH, the straight line KH with its part EH forms a binomial KE + EH. We have BG : GD = KE + EH : EH. The terms of the binomial are KE and EH.

**Step 15.** To show commensurability of the terms: since BD times KH = A^2 and BG times KE = A^2, we have BG times KE = BD times KH. Also apply A^2 to GD to get breadth L, so GD times L = A^2. Then BG times KE = GD times L, giving BG : GD = L : KE, by 6.16. Now from GD times KH = BG times EH, we get GD : BG = EH : KH, so BG : GD = KH : EH. Therefore L : KE = KH : EH. Since BG is commensurable with KE (both related to the rational line A through rational areas, by 10.20), and GD is commensurable with EH (by the parallel construction), the terms of the binomial are commensurable with the terms of the apotome.

**Step 16.** For the order: the square on BG is greater than the square on GD by the square on a straight line either commensurable or incommensurable in length with BG (this determines the order of the apotome, D10.3.1-D10.3.6). Since BG : GD = KH : EH (Step 6) and these are in the same ratio, the square on KH is greater than the square on EH by the square on a straight line bearing the same commensurability relation to KH as the corresponding excess does for BG and GD. By 10.14, since BG, GD, KH, EH are proportional, if the square on BG exceeds the square on GD by the square on a line commensurable with BG, then the square on KH exceeds the square on EH by the square on a line commensurable with KH, and vice versa.

**Step 17.** Furthermore, whichever term of the apotome is commensurable in length with the given rational line determines the order (first through sixth apotome, D10.3.1-D10.3.6). The corresponding term of the binomial will be commensurable in length with the same rational line, since the terms are commensurable with each other (Step 15). Thus by D10.2.1-D10.2.6, the binomial KH is of the same order as the apotome BD.

**Step 18.** To confirm KH is indeed binomial: KE and EH are rational straight lines commensurable in square only (from Steps 9-11 applied to KE and EH as the terms). Their sum KH = KE + EH is therefore a binomial straight line, by 10.36.

**Step 19.** As a verification using 10.112: if KH were a binomial of the order we claim, then by 10.112, the square on A applied to KH would produce an apotome of the same order with commensurable terms in the same ratio. The square on A applied to KH gives breadth BD (since KH times BD = A^2). And indeed BD is the apotome we started with, confirming the result by the converse relationship established in 10.112.

**Step 20.** Therefore the square on the rational straight line A, applied to the apotome BD, produces as breadth the binomial straight line KH, whose terms KE and EH are commensurable with the terms BG and GD of the apotome and in the same ratio; and the binomial KH has the same order as the apotome BD. Q.E.D.
